bib.title: PRE-TRAINED LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS FOR INDUSTRIAL CONTROL
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv:2308.03028v1 [cs.AI], 6 Aug 2023; Microsoft Research Asia technical report)

question: How well can GPT-4, prompted with selected demonstrations and no training, control building HVAC, how well does it generalize across buildings and weather, and which prompt design choices matter?
hypothesis: A pre-trained LLM given few-shot demonstrations can match RL controllers with fewer samples and lower technical debt.
contributions: A training-free method to use foundation models for industrial control across heterogeneous tasks with low technical debt
HVAC control with GPT-4 as an example with positive results
Ablation studies on generalization, demonstration selection and prompt design

method.summary: GPT-4 is the controller. A prompt generator turns building/weather metadata, instructions, retrieved demonstrations (historical, K-means representative, KNN-retrieved expert) and the current state into text; the returned action is executed in the BEAR HVAC simulator. Compared with PPO and an oracle MPC over 240 steps, five seeds.
method.task: HVAC control in the BEAR building simulator via in-context learning

datasets.name: BEAR expert demonstrations (PPO-collected)
datasets.size: 20,000 transitions per scenario (Section 4.2); Section 3 also says a PPO expert is run for 100,000 steps
datasets.split: scenarios = building {OfficeSmall, OfficeMedium, OfficeLarge} x weather {ColdDry, CoolDry, WarmDry, MixedDry}; target OfficeMedium + CoolDry
datasets.preprocessing: states, actions and feedback translated to text; real numbers rounded to integers; actions scaled to integers

models.name: GPT-4
models.architecture: LLM used via API, no fine-tuning

models.name: MPC
models.architecture: oracle with ground-truth outside temperature for next 10 steps

inference.samples: 5 rounds with different seeds per scenario; mean and std reported; 240 steps per run (10 days)
inference.prompting: Few-shot: system-style meta description, heating/cooling instruction, 8 demonstrations (default H2 R2 E4: 2 historical, 2 representative, 4 expert), current state text; optional manual feedback comments per demonstration; actions as integers 0-100 in the prompt
inference.retrieval: Expert demos retrieved by KNN (scikit-learn NearestNeighbors) over Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings of metaTranslator + stateTranslator text; representative demos: K-means (scikit-learn) with 2 clusters, nearest to centres, fixed across steps

parameters.noise_ablation: N(0, std 2) added to outside temperature each step
parameters.demo_notation: H=historical, R=representative, E=expert, followed by count

metrics.name: Reward Mean
metrics.definition: mean per-step reward over 240 steps, reward = (1 - mean |a_i|) + alpha*(1 - sum (t_i - T)^2 / (T n)), T=22 C; mean over 5 seeds

eval.protocol: 240 steps, 5 seeds, mean and std reported; no significance test

prompts.text: You are the HVAC administrator responsible for managing a building of type Office Medium located in Buffalo, where the climate is Hot and Dry.
Before initiating actions, it is advisable to first offer feedback on the quality of all the provided demonstrations to further improve the comprehension of control logics derived from them.

prompts.purpose: instructionTranslator (heating mode), items 3-4 are the Task Instructions
prompts.text: 3. If room temperature is higher than the target temperature, the larger the difference between room temperature and the target temperature, the lower the action should be. 4. If room temperature is lower than the target temperature, the larger the difference between room temperature and the target temperature, the higher the action should be.

results.claim: Authors conclude GPT-4 is comparable to RL with fewer samples and lower technical debt
results.note: Abstract: 'GPT-4 achieves a performance comparable to RL methods but with fewer samples and lower technical debt'. No sample-count comparison is measured.

limits: Single target scenario (OfficeMedium/CoolDry); other scenarios only supply demonstrations.
GPT-4 version, temperature, max tokens, reward alpha not stated; no code release mentioned.
The 'fewer samples' claim is not measured: PPO experts trained 100M steps are used as demonstrations (20,000 transitions collected), so GPT-4 depends on PPO-generated data except Group F.
Authors concede LLMs lack self-learning from interaction; proposed demonstration scoring/generation approaches have no results ('will be updated in the future version').
Authors' hypothesis that self-comment hurt because the instruction was too simple is untested.
Table 7 '+' ratings are qualitative judgements, not measurements.
Only 5 seeds and no significance test; many differences are within one std.
Abstract and conclusion state results across 'different scenarios' and 'generalization' while only one target is evaluated.
